answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a bond before bidding for work, whether it serves a harbor, maps a mesa, or monitors a reef. Bonds stay locked through a dispute window and are slashed for provable non-delivery under the job contract. Creating names is cheap, but activating a thousand bidders requires a thousand bonds, tying up the attacker’s capital and putting it at risk whenever a fake agent takes work and fails to deliver.
